clause_evidence.reasoning: Samples comprehensively test student ability to identify and select correct representations of circles, half-circles, and quarter-circles from multiple choice options. Students demonstrate representational knowledge by recognizing which option correctly represents the described shape across numerous samples.

Samples test descriptive understanding through property identification (corners, sides, straight edges) and through relational description (how shapes are formed by dividing circles). Students must apply descriptive knowledge of shape characteristics to answer questions correctly.

Circles appear directly in samples involving property-based identification, rotation invariance, and as the whole from which halves and quarters are derived. Multiple samples explicitly test circle recognition and its distinguishing characteristics.

Half-circles are tested in multiple contexts: identification by name when a circle is divided into 2 equal parts, identification when described as exactly half of a circle, and comparison with quarter-circles. All core aspects of half-circle representation and description are present.

Quarter-circles are tested through identification when a circle is divided into 4 equal parts, when described as exactly one quarter of a circle, through rotation invariance testing, and through comparison with half-circles and fractions. All essential quarter-circle concepts are represented.

competency_alignment.rationale: Samples collectively test all required elements: identification of circles, half-circles, and quarter-circles; property-based description; and understanding of fractional relationships between shapes.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Samples demonstrate student understanding of what represents each shape (circles, half-circles, quarter-circles) and test ability to describe them through properties and relationships.

decomposition.reasoning: The printed requirements fully decompose the competency statement. Each component (represent, describe, circles, half circles, quarter circles) is explicitly addressed in the requirement list and represented in samples.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: While all shape types are present, approximately 18 of 22 samples are near-duplicate or substantially repetitive versions of a small number of core question templates. This reduces actual coverage diversity and testing breadth compared to sample count.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Content is suitable for Grade 2, Quarter 1. Shape identification by properties is developmentally appropriate, and fractions (half, quarter) are introduced at this level for geometric decomposition.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only 3-4 distinct question types appear across 22 samples: identification by properties, identification by division count, rotation invariance testing, and comparative edge counting. Most samples repeat these patterns verbatim or with minor option reordering.
